claims.assertion: This is a dangerous-driving allegation (speeding, hard braking, overtaking on the shoulder), so per SAFE-2 the case must be escalated to a human rather than auto-adjudicated; the driver does not oppose escalation on a SAFE-2 basis.

The GPS record shows the trip was run efficiently and without any detour: actual distance 8.3 km versus 8.4 km optimal (-0.1 km, -1%), so the ride was not extended and the rider's fixed $20.85 RydeX fare was neither inflated nor altered by any routing choice.

The trip took 12.7 min against the 13.8 min estimate (-1.1 min), which is consistent with normal progress on the route and inconsistent with a ride consisting of sustained speeding and hard braking from pickup (21:22) to drop-off (21:34).

The only in-app messages are the rider's pickup-location note and the driver's ETA reply; neither message, nor the rider's conduct during the trip, contains any complaint about speed or driving, and the rider never told the driver to slow down.

The driver's account record shows 963 trips in 90 days, a 4.85 rating and 0 disputes (0 upheld, route 0, no-show 0), so there is no documented pattern of dangerous or rule-breaking driving that the allegation would corroborate.

Because the allegation is unbacked by any GPS, timeline or chat fact in the file, no monetary remedy is computable against the driver: the fare is a fixed RydeX quote with no fare facts in the file, so the correct outcome is no refund of the fare pending human review.

weaknesses: The rider's complaint is a first-hand account of feeling unsafe, and SAFE-2 sends dangerous-driving allegations to a human; I cannot rebut the rider's perception with the records available — the file has no telematics (no speed, acceleration or harsh-braking data), only F1 (distance) and F2 (duration), which speak to route and time and not to driving style.

The rider's account is not contradicted by the chat: F3-F5 show only two messages and no complaint, but the absence of a complaint during an unsafe-feeling ride is not proof the ride was safe, so F6's 'never complained' relies on the driver's own post-trip statement and carries little weight on its own.

Timing cuts both ways: F2's 12.7 min against a 13.8 min estimate is only about 8% faster and does not exclude short bursts of speeding on part of the route, which the rider could have experienced even if the overall trip was not quicker than estimated.

The rider's profile (F7: 3.3-year account, rating 4.6, 0 disputes in 90 days, 0 upheld) shows a clean history and no history of unfounded complaints, which a judge may weigh in favour of the rider's credibility.

RIDER: Your dispute on trip B-0046 has been passed to a Ryde reviewer. No decision has been made yet: nothing has been refunded or charged as part of this review. The reviewer will look at the messages exchanged and both parties' accounts of what happened; the trip record, including the parts that are missing from it. Ryde will contact you once the review is complete.

DRIVER: The dispute on trip B-0046 has been passed to a Ryde reviewer. No decision has been made yet, and nothing changes on your account or earnings as part of this review. The reviewer will look at the messages exchanged and both parties' accounts of what happened; the trip record, including the parts that are missing from it. Ryde will contact you once the review is complete.

ruling.recommended_action: Send the file to a human safety reviewer as a dangerous-driving allegation under SAFE-2; treat the fixed RydeX fare as unchanged (no refund computed) and take account action only if the reviewer substantiates the report.
ruling.reasoning:
This is a dispute type of safety, and the rider's complaint alleges speeding, hard braking and shoulder overtaking — that is a dangerous-driving allegation, so SAFE-2 applies and the case cannot be auto-decided; both advocates concede the mechanism and request escalation [F6][SAFE-2]. The trace's ✓ element (SAFE-1 screening: complaint filed as a safety incident) and the allowed-outcome list (escalate) also bind this file [SAFE-1].

What happened: pickup 21:22, drop-off 21:34 on a RydeX Jurong East MRT → NUS trip; the rider reports being scared and feeling unsafe throughout [F1]. The only quantitative records are F1 (8.3 km actual vs 8.4 km optimal, -0.1 km / -1%) and F2 (12.7 min vs 13.8 min estimate, -1.1 min) — these settle route and duration only; they contain no speed, acceleration, braking or shoulder-use data, so they neither corroborate nor rebut the driving-style allegation [F1][F2][SAFE-2]. A missing telematics slice and a null traffic lookup are gaps, not evidence for either side [F1][F2][SAFE-2].

The chat is complete (2 messages, both timestamped) and contains only the rider's pickup note and the driver's ETA reply — no complaint about speed or driving [F3][F4][F5][SAFE-1]. Silence there is not proof the ride was safe, and F6 (the driver's post-trip written statement that he drove normally and the rider never complained) is a party statement, not a system record of driving style, so it carries little weight on the safety question [F6][SAFE-1].

Profiles do not decide this: F7 (rider clean, 0 disputes/0 upheld in 90 d) and F8 (driver 675 d, 4.85, 963 trips, 0 disputes/0 upheld) cut both ways and cannot resolve a first-hand safety report [F7][F8][RD-6].

On money: RydeX is a fixed quote and the file contains no fare fact, so no refund is computable from F1/F2 and none is proposed; both sides concede no fare ruling is sought [F1][F2][SAFE-2]. RD-1/RD-2 are not engaged by the distance record (no off-route segment fact exists), so no segment_findings are recorded [F1][RD-1][RD-2].

rejected_claims.reason: Profile facts (F8: 963 trips, 4.85 rating, 0 disputes/0 upheld in 90 d) never decide a case alone and cannot disprove a first-hand safety report; RD-6's account-flag precondition (an upheld case plus prior upheld route dispute) is not met, so F8 yields no outcome either way [F8][RD-6].

The request for 'no refund of the fare pending human review' mischaracterises the outcome: RydeX is a fixed quote with no fare fact in the file, so there is nothing to refund or affirm — the case is escalated under SAFE-2, and no_action is not an available outcome on the trace [F1][F2][SAFE-2].

The inference that no in-app complaint (F3, F4, F5) plus the driver's statement (F6) shows the driving was safe is rejected: silence during an allegedly unsafe ride is not proof of safety, and F6 is a party statement, not a system record of driving style [F3][F4][F5][F6][SAFE-1].

Correct but non-dispositive: F1 (8.3 km actual vs 8.4 km optimal) speaks only to route length; with no off-route segment fact in the file, RD-1/RD-2 are not engaged and the record answers nothing about speed, braking or shoulder use [F1][RD-1][RD-2].
F2 (12.7 min vs 13.8 min, -1.1 min) is an end-to-end average and cannot exclude short bursts of speeding or hard braking, so it does not contradict the rider's account [F2][SAFE-2].

The absence of traffic/incident records is not corroboration of the speeding allegation; a missing record is treated as a gap, never as evidence for either side, so no finding follows from it [F1][F2][SAFE-2].

Reliance on F7/F8 to support or discount credibility is rejected: profiles never decide a case alone, and RD-6's flag precondition is not satisfied (no upheld case here), so no account action follows from either profile [F7][F8][RD-6].

ruling.evidence_gap: No telematics of driving style anywhere in the file: no speed, acceleration, harsh-braking or shoulder-use record, and no traffic/incident facts on the optimal route; the file therefore cannot settle whether the alleged dangerous driving occurred, which SAFE-2 requires a human to review.
ruling.escalation_reason: Dangerous-driving allegation (speeding, hard braking, shoulder overtaking) under SAFE-2 with no telematics or traffic record to settle it; the human reviewer should read the rider's complaint against F1 (8.3 km vs 8.4 km optimal, -1%), F2 (12.7 min vs 13.8 min, -1.1 min), the complete chat F3–F5, and the driver's post-trip statement F6 (party statement, not a system record). Report paths for the rider: 995 if medical help is needed, driver's commercial motor insurance for a medical claim, RydeHELP for the report [F1][F2][F3][F4][F5][F6].

claims.assertion: The rider's complaint states the driver was speeding, braking hard and overtaking on the shoulder, and that she was scared and felt unsafe; this is an allegation of dangerous driving, which must go to a human and cannot be auto-decided.
The safety allegation is the substance of the dispute, so the correct action is escalate with a fact summary, and I do not seek a fare ruling on the ride itself.

The record contains no traffic or incident evidence on the optimal route (get_traffic_facts returned none), so nothing in the file rebuts the rider's account of unsafe driving from the road-conditions side.

The chat record is complete (2 messages, all timestamped) and shows no complaint or message from the rider in the car, but the absence of a contemporaneous complaint does not defeat a safety report; the driver's written statement asserting he drove normally is a post-trip self-serving claim.

Neither profile shows any prior dispute (rider 0 in 90 days, driver 0 in 90 days with 263 trips-equivalent record of 963 trips), so the file gives no basis to discount the rider's report on history grounds; profile facts are not used to decide the safety question itself.

weaknesses: The rider's speeding/braking/overtaking allegation appears only in her own complaint; there is no GPS record of speed, hard braking, harsh acceleration or shoulder use, and F1/F2 show a normal-looking trip (8.3 km vs 8.4 km optimal, 12.7 min vs 13.8 min estimated), so the driver will argue the telemetry contradicts the complaint.

The chat is complete and contains no complaint from the rider during or after the trip (F3, F4, F5), and the rider was reportedly on the phone the whole way (F6), which the driver will use to argue no concern was voiced at the time.
The rider has no route, no-show or other upheld disputes and the driver has a clean record (F7, F8), which the driver will cite to argue this is an isolated, unverified account.

The complaint is a narrative without supporting evidence such as photos, a witness or a police report; if the human reviewer requires corroboration, the case may end without any account action against the driver.

claims.assertion: This is a dangerous-driving allegation (speeding, hard braking, overtaking on the shoulder), so per SAFE-2 the case must be escalated to a human rather than auto-adjudicated; the driver does not oppose escalation on a SAFE-2 basis.

The GPS record shows the trip was run efficiently and without any detour: actual distance 8.3 km versus 8.4 km optimal (-0.1 km, -1%), so the ride was not extended and the rider's fixed $20.85 RydeX fare was neither inflated nor altered by any routing choice.

The trip took 12.7 min against the 13.8 min estimate (-1.1 min), which is consistent with normal progress on the route and inconsistent with a ride consisting of sustained speeding and hard braking from pickup (21:22) to drop-off (21:34).

The only in-app messages are the rider's pickup-location note and the driver's ETA reply; neither message, nor the rider's conduct during the trip, contains any complaint about speed or driving, and the rider never told the driver to slow down.

The driver's account record shows 963 trips in 90 days, a 4.85 rating and 0 disputes (0 upheld, route 0, no-show 0), so there is no documented pattern of dangerous or rule-breaking driving that the allegation would corroborate.

Because the allegation is unbacked by any GPS, timeline or chat fact in the file, no monetary remedy is computable against the driver: the fare is a fixed RydeX quote with no fare facts in the file, so the correct outcome is no refund of the fare pending human review.

weaknesses: The rider's complaint is a first-hand account of feeling unsafe, and SAFE-2 sends dangerous-driving allegations to a human; I cannot rebut the rider's perception with the records available — the file has no telematics (no speed, acceleration or harsh-braking data), only F1 (distance) and F2 (duration), which speak to route and time and not to driving style.

The rider's account is not contradicted by the chat: F3-F5 show only two messages and no complaint, but the absence of a complaint during an unsafe-feeling ride is not proof the ride was safe, so F6's 'never complained' relies on the driver's own post-trip statement and carries little weight on its own.

Timing cuts both ways: F2's 12.7 min against a 13.8 min estimate is only about 8% faster and does not exclude short bursts of speeding on part of the route, which the rider could have experienced even if the overall trip was not quicker than estimated.

The rider's profile (F7: 3.3-year account, rating 4.6, 0 disputes in 90 days, 0 upheld) shows a clean history and no history of unfounded complaints, which a judge may weigh in favour of the rider's credibility.

points.response: Agreed on the mechanism: a dangerous-driving allegation goes to a human under SAFE-2, so the parties are not in dispute that the case is escalated rather than auto-decided — my client's report is a first-hand account (F6 context, rider complaint) and is not something the driver's post-trip statement can resolve.

This is true but irrelevant to a safety dispute: F1 shows only distance (8.3 km vs 8.4 km optimal), which speaks to routing and not to speed, braking or shoulder use, so it cannot answer the rider's complaint.

F2 (12.7 min vs 13.8 min estimated) is an end-to-end average and cannot exclude short bursts of speeding or hard braking, which is exactly what the rider reported; the driver's own admitted weakness says this timing 'does not exclude short bursts of speeding'.

The chat is complete (2 messages, all timestamped, F5) and shows no complaint, but silence during a ride the rider says she was frightened on is not proof the driving was safe, and F6 is the driver's own post-trip statement, which under the system's precedence rules is a statement rather than a system record of driving style.

F8 shows 0 disputes and 0 upheld for the driver, which at most means no prior complaint was ever recorded — a clean record cannot disprove a new first-hand report, and profile facts may support an outcome but never decide the safety question.

Conceded as to money: I do not seek any fare refund, because RydeX is a fixed quote and the file returned no fare facts, so the escalation I ask for is a human safety review (and whatever account action that review supports), not a refund computed from F1/F2.

Conceded: the rider's complaint is an allegation of dangerous driving, and SAFE-2 routes such allegations to a human; my client does not resist escalation on that basis, but nothing in the file supplies any corroboration beyond the complaint itself, so escalation is the whole of the outcome, not a finding against the driver.

Agreed that the outcome is escalate and that no fare ruling is sought; but the fact summary handed to the human reviewer must include F1 (8.3 km actual vs 8.4 km optimal, -1%) and F2 (12.7 min vs 13.8 min estimated), which record a trip that was run slightly short and slightly quicker than the optimal route and estimate, not an erratic one.

Accept that get_traffic_facts returned no records, but the absence of traffic data is not evidence of driving style; the only quantitative record of the ride is F1 and F2, which show the trip matched the optimal route and finished 1.1 min inside the estimate, and no policy clause treats a missing traffic slice as corroboration of a speeding allegation.

Conceded in part: F6 is the driver's own post-trip statement and I do not rest my case on it; however F3-F5 show the rider never sent any complaint in-app during or after the trip, and under RD-5's standard (system records and the rider's own written messages outweigh a party's unsupported narrative) that silence is the strongest contemporaneous item on the driver's side.

Agreed that profiles decide nothing here; F8 (963 trips in 90 days, rating 4.85, 0 disputes, 0 upheld) is offered only to show the alleged speeding, hard braking and shoulder overtaking form no documented pattern, and it cannot support any account action against the driver.

My escalation request stands unchanged for the same reason as the opposing side's: SAFE-2 sends dangerous-driving allegations to a human, and neither side has produced telematics of speed, acceleration or shoulder use, so no automated finding for or against the driver is possible on this file.
